editorial.summary: Steve Lee, Bill Poon and Valentin host in the studio while David Choe participates only through an early speakerphone call. That call immediately supplies the episode's strongest privacy lesson: David objects when a private will-related conversation is exposed without warning, then endorses the cast continuing the show without him. He describes intensive therapy, attention practice, food experiments and Steve's prospective rap album before leaving the call. The studio then moves from friendship anxiety into Peggy Kane, electronic voice phenomena, reverse speech, reptilians, lower astral planes, dream portals and alleged suppressed human abilities. Steve and Valentin add haunting stories, including experiences involving hallucinogens and a young sibling. The record preserves all of these claims as beliefs or reported perceptions while refusing to present them as verified supernatural or medical facts. A discussion of schizophrenia is especially important: the speakers wonder whether voices could be paranormal, but this is medically unsupported and can stigmatize people with psychosis. The title phrase emerges directly from that debate. The Sewol ferry disaster shifts the conversation toward obedience, Korean parenting, drowning and other distressing deaths. Alex then explains the show's labor transition, why commitment mattered more than preexisting technical skill, and how DVDASA began. The final half mixes Critter and David origin stories, creative-work philosophy, household nicknames, exercise, reproductive and racialized jokes, conflicting cast-origin memories, a secret studio redesign, Bigfoot, sexualized show-format ideas, camping, Steve's album, nail art and trivia. Every idea is retained. The transcript keeps literal speech separate from annotations: it does not replace 'health podcast' or 'Grammy Boys,' append a legal name to Dan the Automator, or insert a Reddit explanation into a spoken date. Two empty zero-duration records are the only valid cleaner drops. David's phone presence ends around 16 minutes; with zero diarized turns and zero identity windows, no line receives a published speaker name.
